correctness.rationale: The bounded maximum/minimum principle confines all real stationary states to [0,1]. With r=(3−√3)/12 and m=√3/8, each of three disjoint root intervals has |g′|≥m and inverse Lipschitz ≤1/m. For any root code, T_s= (g|J_s)^{-1}(−dΔv) maps the complete supnorm product B_s into itself since 2d*(1+2r)=rm, and contracts with factor 4d/m<(4−√3)/13<1. Any bounded stationary point has |g(u_j)|≤2d; the complementary gaps in [0,1] have |g|≥rm, so no coordinate can be outside root intervals. Consequently each profile is the unique contraction fixed point for exactly one code. Finite-iteration locality and uniformly decaying contraction error yield product-topology continuity; shift equivariance is exact. Independent symbolic values and boundary derivatives were checked; periodic examples do not replace bi-infinite contraction proof.
